text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Economic competition in the region is hotting up President Ong Teng Cheong tells parliament.
- An armada of Japanese patrol boats thwarts a bid by Hongkong and Taiwanese activists to land on the Diaoyu islands, a disputed archipelago in the East China Sea.
- A growing number of manufacturers single out price as the most crucial factor to winning more orders from overseas buyers.
- Property giant DBS Land may be squaring up to buy Malaysian-listed Hospital Pantai's 19 percent stake in listed health care group Parkway Holdings.
- Thailand's central bank downgrades key economic forecasts for this year but predicts the limping economy will bottom out in mid-year and begin recovering in the fourth quarter.
- The new resale levy will cost Housing Board dwellers as much as Singapore $120,000 more to buy a second new HDB flat.
- Singapore investors eye hotels in Thailand and in other regional capitals, say hotel brokers and consultants.
- Rewards in Singapore should depend only on ability and performance, and not on race, language or religion, President Ong Teng Cheong says.
- Two shipping associations in Port Klang call on companies in Malaysia to stop using Singapore's port and use local ports instead.
- Natsteel Ltd, just weeks away from listing its electronics subsidiary, is raising Singapore $272 million for more investment in its traditional steel business.
- Aztech Systems is "firmly placed to resume growth and profitability" after returning to the black in last year's second half, says company president Michael Mun in the company's annual report.
- Industrial products company Bousteadco reports a hefty 57 percent fall in net profit to Singapore $1.52 million for its financial year ended March 31, 1997.
- The Bank of Thailand's latest rescue plan for the country's biggest finance firm, the debt-laden Finance One, will not solve the crisis of bad loans facing the financial sector, analysts say.
- Singapore-listed Osprey Maritime signs a Singapore $1.3 billion loan to finance its purchase of the Gotaas-Larsen Shipping Corp.
